Format numbers as ordinals in a gt table

Source: R/gt_fmt_rank.R
gt_fmt_rank.Rd

Turns plain integers into ordinals: 1 becomes 1st, 2 becomes 2nd, 23 becomes 23rd. The suffix can be rendered as superscript, which is the usual treatment in a ranked column.

Usage

gt_fmt_rank(gt_object, columns, superscript = TRUE, suffix_size = "0.7em")

Arguments

gt_object

A gt table object to modify.

columns

The column or columns to format.

superscript

Logical. Should the suffix be rendered as superscript? Defaults to TRUE.

suffix_size

Character. The size of the suffix, as a CSS size. Defaults to "0.7em".

Value

Returns a modified gt table with ordinal formatting applied.

Details

Teens are handled correctly, so 11, 12 and 13 take "th" and not "st", "nd" and "rd". Values that are not numeric are left alone.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(gt)

ranked <- data.frame(
  model = rownames(head(mtcars, 5)),
  place = 1:5
)

gt(ranked) %>% gt_fmt_rank(place)

# flat, without the superscript
gt(ranked) %>% gt_fmt_rank(place, superscript = FALSE)
} # }
